title: The radio incident that ended the Milwaukee job
summary: Roy sang drunkenly on a radio broadcast, was cut off the air, and the manager paid him to leave town.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Was that the first time you started to sing, or had you done it before?

Well, I guess that's when I... No, I'd learned. Just I didn't tell about that, you know. I used to get out and do a lot of things I had no business doing. Well, anyway, I knew I wasn't no singer neither; you know, it wasn't one of those things where this is what I wanted to do. But it just so happened, you know. And I think I was singing "I'll Be Glad When You're Dead, You Rascal, You," you know. Not knowing... Because I used to drink a lot then. Not knowing, I sang, "I'll glad when you're dead, no more pussy will you claim" -- you know. Click! We went off the air, you know. So I didn't know nothin' about it, until I got out the neighborhood, you know, and the cat said, "Man, they cut you off, and you know what you sing now."
When I turned in that night, all that wires that they had strung up was all taken down. So the manager called me, and he said, "You know, all the fellows like you. You're a

nice little fellow. But I don't know how they're gonna take that when they find out what happened. So I'm going to give you two weeks salary, and you'd better take it out of town, because I don't think they'll be too happy about this." That's when I left.
